Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary TacTile is an engine building abstract strategy game where you move pawns on a board to trigger bonus actions from your tableau of cards. Your goal is to cross the modular 4 color board and score both your pawns in your opponents home first. As you advance across the board you can gain resources and buy colorful action cards. Action cards are permanently added to your tableau and can give one free action per turn, but you must activate them by landing on a matching color tile. Build your action engine and use clever positioning to activate your cards in this combo-tastic game of tile tactics! 4 player mode is a competitive 2v2 team battle with special cooperative abilities including the ability to push your ally's pawn and swap cards with your ally. The "convert" rule. - You may exhaust two available actions for a free action of your choice. - Available actions: activated unexhausted action cards - basic actions are not available for convert. - Free action options: MOVE, GAIN, PUSH, SWAP, BUY, RESET ************************************************** NEW GAMEMODE - March 4th -2026 CLASSIC MODE - no CONVERT action - the market is now a fixed market - The deck into broken into three decks based on type (MOVE, GAIN, PUSH) and there are always 2 of each type in the market. When a card is bought it is replaced from its respective deck. OVERDRIVE MODE - Normal rules apply. [Rating: 4/10] Abstract grid-traversal with powerup cards that you can buy and recharge based on the colours of squares that you visit. Felt a bit too unbalanced by whether there happened to be a good funnel of repeating colours into a corner; that it helps the attacker more than the defender. [Update: The developer has offered to play the game with me on BGA to correct my view of its balance, but I've declined.]

[Rating: 4/10] Cute. I wonder about the depth of strategy here, as some actions are much more important than others, and each player generally wants to set up the same action sequence from one game to the next. Because the game is head to head, small moments of luck in the card market have a outsized impact on play.

[Rating: 5/10] The gameplay seemed interesting at first, but then the game turned into a slog of Moving your pieces and Pushing your opponent's. It went on too long as a result. Perhaps if the cards cost more resources there would be fewer activations and a quicker game?

[Rating: 5/10] Great concept that just didn't quite hit for me. I think having luck be a factor at all here really hampers the game. Without it, though, there's likely an easily optimized route for upgrading and doing stuff through the course of the game. Not sure what the solution would be.
